Working notes:

- Small online claims showed repeated fraud in this sample: CLM-7001 (auto), CLM-7006 (home), and CLM-7007 (auto) were approved but later audited as fraudulent. Treat “no apparent fraud indicators” and low amount as insufficient; apply enhanced verification to online small claims.
- Online large health (CLM-7005), phone large home (CLM-7002), paper large home (CLM-7009), and phone small health (CLM-7004) were approved and settled successfully.
- Every rejection in this sample was later appealed and found valid: CLM-7003 and CLM-7010 (health, phone, large) and CLM-7008 (auto, phone, large). Avoid rejecting solely because documentation is not immediately described or because the amount is large; request/complete supporting verification first.
- Validate incident details, repair/treatment estimates, policy eligibility, and supporting documentation before deciding.
- Current evidence supports targeted scrutiny of small online filings, not blanket rejection by category, channel, or amount.

Working notes:

- Strong fraud pattern in small online claims: CLM-7001, CLM-7006, CLM-7007, CLM-7011, CLM-7015, CLM-7016, CLM-7018, CLM-7017, CLM-7019, and CLM-7020 were all later audited as fraudulent. Treat low amount, plausible incident details, and “no apparent indicators” as insufficient. Require enhanced verification before approval, including eligibility, incident/treatment validation, estimates or billing, and supporting documents.
- Do not approve a small online claim merely because it appears legitimate on available information; incomplete or undescribed checks are a material warning. Where verification is absent, hold for enhanced review or reject according to procedure.
- Successful examples include CLM-7002 (large home, phone), CLM-7004 (small health, phone), CLM-7005 (large health, online), CLM-7009 (large home, paper), CLM-7012 (small health, phone), CLM-7013 (large auto, paper), and CLM-7014 (large home, phone).
- Every rejection in this sample was later validated as fraudulent, including CLM-7003, CLM-7008, CLM-7010, CLM-7011, CLM-7015, CLM-7016, and CLM-7018. Nonetheless, decisions should be based on completed verification rather than amount alone or a category/channel rule.
- Large claims are not inherently fraudulent; complete supporting verification before approval. Avoid rejecting solely because a claim is large or documentation is not immediately described—request and assess it first.
- Current evidence supports very high scrutiny of small online filings, while phone, paper, large, and other categories still require ordinary case-specific validation.

Working notes:

- Several small online claims were later confirmed fraudulent: CLM-7001, 7006, 7007, 7011, 7015, 7016, 7017, 7018, 7019, 7020, 7022, 7023, 7025, and 7026. Low amount, plausible details, and no visible indicators are insufficient. Require enhanced verification of eligibility, incident/treatment, estimates or billing, and supporting documents.
- Do not approve when required checks are incomplete or undescribed. However, distinguish “not approvable yet” from outright rejection: hold/request documentation and complete verification where procedure permits. Unsupported rejection caused valid claims to be rejected in CLM-7021, 7024, 7027, 7028, and 7030.
- Large claims are not inherently fraudulent. Valid examples include CLM-7002, 7005, 7009, 7013, 7014, 7021, 7024, and 7030. Complete case-specific verification before approval; do not reject solely due to amount, channel, or missing details that can be requested.
- Phone claims can be valid across sizes and categories (CLM-7004, 7012, 7014, 7027, 7028, 7029, 7030); paper claims can be valid (CLM-7009, 7013, 7021); large online claims can be valid (CLM-7005, 7024). CLM-7029 was a valid large phone claim approved after appropriate checks.
- Every rejection in the earlier sample was fraud-confirmed, but recent valid appeals show rejection is not itself evidence of fraud. Use evidence and completed verification, not amount/category/channel rules.
- Maintain very high scrutiny for small online filings, while applying ordinary, documented validation to all other claims. When fraud indicators remain after verification, reject according to procedure; otherwise approve or continue review.

Working notes:

- Confirmed fraudulent claims include CLM-7001, 7006, 7007, 7011, 7015–7020, 7022, 7023, 7025, 7026, 7034, 7037, and 7039. Fraud can occur in any amount, category, or channel. Small online claims warrant heightened scrutiny, but size/channel alone is never proof.
- Valid claims rejected without adequate verification include CLM-7021, 7024, 7027, 7028, 7030, 7031–7033, 7035, 7036, 7038, and 7040. Rejection is not evidence of fraud; appeals and audits demonstrate that valid claims occur across health, auto, and home coverage, and across phone, paper, and online filing.
- Large claims are not inherently fraudulent. Valid examples include CLM-7002, 7005, 7009, 7013, 7014, 7021, 7024, 7029, 7031, 7033, and 7036. Small claims also require evidence-based review.
- Do not reject solely because of amount, category, filing channel, plausible details, or incomplete information that can be requested. Distinguish “not approvable yet” from outright rejection: place on hold/request documents and complete verification where procedure permits.
- Before approval, verify eligibility/coverage, incident and timing, treatment or damage, and estimates, invoices, or repair/billing records as applicable. Document what checks were completed.
- If required checks are incomplete, do not approve yet; request evidence or continue review. If verification establishes fraud, reject according to procedure. If evidence supports validity and no fraud indicators remain, approve.

Working notes:

- Confirmed fraudulent claims include CLM-7001, 7006, 7007, 7011, 7015–7020, 7022, 7023, 7025, 7026, 7034, 7037, 7039, 7042, 7045, 7047, and 7049. Fraud can occur at any amount, in any coverage category, and through any filing channel. Small online claims merit scrutiny, but amount or channel alone is never proof.
- Valid claims wrongly rejected include CLM-7021, 7024, 7027, 7028, 7030, 7031–7033, 7035, 7036, 7038, 7040, 7041, 7043, 7044, 7046, 7048, and 7050. Valid claims occur across health, auto, and home coverage; phone, paper, and online filing; and all claim sizes.
- A rejection is not evidence of fraud. Do not reject solely because of amount, category, channel, plausible details, or missing information that can be requested. Distinguish “not approvable yet” from rejection: place the claim on hold and request documents where procedure permits.
- Before approval, verify eligibility/coverage, incident and timing, treatment or damage, and relevant estimates, invoices, repair, or billing records. Document completed checks.
- If checks are incomplete, continue review or request evidence; do not approve or make a fraud finding prematurely. If verification establishes fraud, reject according to procedure. If evidence supports validity and no fraud indicators remain, approve.

Working notes:

- Confirmed fraudulent claims include CLM-7001, 7006, 7007, 7011, 7015–7020, 7022, 7023, 7025, 7026, 7034, 7037, 7039, 7042, 7045, 7047, 7049, 7051, 7053, 7056, 7058, and 7059. Fraud can occur at any amount, coverage category, or filing channel. Amount, category, channel, plausible details, or missing information alone are never proof.
- Valid claims wrongly rejected include CLM-7021, 7024, 7027, 7028, 7030, 7031–7033, 7035, 7036, 7038, 7040, 7041, 7043, 7044, 7046, 7048, 7050, 7052, 7054, 7055, 7057, and 7060. Valid claims occur across health, auto, and home coverage; phone, paper, and online filing; and all claim sizes.
- A rejection is not evidence of fraud. Do not reject solely because of amount, category, channel, plausible details, or incomplete information. Distinguish “not approvable yet” from rejection: place the claim on hold and request documents where procedure permits.
- Before approval, verify eligibility/coverage, incident and timing, treatment or damage, and relevant estimates, invoices, repair, or billing records. Document completed checks.
- If checks are incomplete, continue review or request evidence; do not approve or make a fraud finding prematurely. If verification establishes fraud, reject according to procedure. If evidence supports validity and no fraud indicators remain, approve.
- Recent errors reinforce that even large claims and apparently suspicious home claims may be valid, while some small online claims may be fraudulent. Use evidence-based investigation, not heuristics.

Working notes:

- Confirmed fraudulent claims include CLM-7001, 7006, 7007, 7011, 7015–7020, 7022, 7023, 7025, 7026, 7034, 7037, 7039, 7042, 7045, 7047, 7049, 7051, 7053, 7056, 7058, 7059, 7062, 7064, 7065, and 7070.
- Valid claims wrongly rejected include CLM-7021, 7024, 7027, 7028, 7030, 7031–7033, 7035, 7036, 7038, 7040, 7041, 7043, 7044, 7046, 7048, 7050, 7052, 7054, 7055, 7057, 7060, 7061, 7063, and 7066–7069.
- Fraud and validity occur at every amount, coverage category, and filing channel. Large claims, small claims, paper, phone, and online submissions are not inherently suspicious or trustworthy.
- A rejection is not evidence of fraud. Do not reject solely because of amount, category, channel, plausible details, or missing information. When procedure permits, place incomplete claims on hold and request documentation; a hold is not approval.
- Before approval, verify eligibility/coverage, incident and timing, treatment or damage, and relevant estimates, invoices, repair, or billing records. Document each check.
- Do not approve merely because the claim appears routine or because only routine checks remain. Recent audits found approved claims CLM-7062, 7064, and 7070 fraudulent.
- If evidence is incomplete, continue review or request evidence. If verification establishes fraud, reject according to procedure. Approve only when validity is supported and fraud indicators have been resolved.
